mathematical_checks: Interval.Contains means lo <= scale*x <= hi; positive denominator floor and negated floor implement outward rounding, including negative numerators.
Complex addition, subtraction, exact rational multiplication and integration preserve rectangular enclosures at the same scale.
normSqLo bounds the true scaled squared norm from below; normSqHi bounds it from above. ratioCheck uses denominator upper bound times num^2 strictly below numerator lower bound times den^2.

checkAt requires positive scale, positive target denominator and positive input denominators with nonzero complex centers. Target numerator is a natural number, so the nonnegative-target norm-square implication applies.

productBoxes encloses ascending coefficients of the monic product of X-c. integrateAux divides coefficient k by k+1 and prepends zero, giving precisely its zero-constant primitive. evalBoxes uses the corresponding ascending Horner rule.

The mathematical prescribedPolynomial is antiderivative(q)/q(0), with q the monic critical product. The checker encloses antiderivative(q)(c) and q(0)*c, so its ratio test is for this exact polynomial.
Nonzero centers imply q(0) != 0 algebraically; a numerical q(0) enclosure need not exclude zero, since the ratio check only uses its conservative upper squared norm.

prescribedPolynomial_critical_iff proves derivative vanishes iff the point occurs in the supplied list; repeated centers are permitted. natDegree_prescribedPolynomial proves exact degree length+1, so there are no missing exterior roots.

The generic checker permits an empty center list, correctly defining degree-one P=X with vacuous critical bounds. Concrete high-degree theorems must and can establish the explicit list length; checker soundness itself does not falsely assert degree >=2.
